title: An Astronaut Just Spotted a Piece of the Moon in Madagascar

scenes.text: An astronaut just spotted a piece of the Moon in Madagascar.
scenes.keywords: astronaut looking out space station window earth

scenes.text: From the Space Station, it's a bright white patch of rock, forty square miles wide.
It's anorthosite. The same rock that makes the bright parts of the Moon glow at night.
scenes.keywords: full moon close up craters bright

scenes.text: On the Moon, it crystallised out of an ocean of magma four billion years ago and floated to the top, forming the crust.
Real Moon samples are so rare that NASA studies rocks like these instead. So next full Moon, look at the white parts. Madagascar has the same thing.

description:
An astronaut on the International Space Station has photographed a patch of Moon-like rock in southern Madagascar.
The bright white formation covers about 40 square miles and is made of anorthosite, the same rock that forms the Moon's bright, more than four-billion-year-old highlands. Earth's patch is at least 600 million years old, and because Apollo samples are so limited, NASA geologists study rocks like these to understand the Moon's crust.
Where on Earth would you most like to see a landscape that looks like another world?
thumbnail_text: A PIECE OF THE MOON... IN MADAGASCAR
first_comment: Bonus: a second patch of the same rock sits about 40 miles north and may once have been joined to this one before Gondwana tore them apart. Where on Earth would you go to feel like you're on another planet?
